headline: The Sandy Hook Starter Pack
subhead: Key geographic landmarks, parks, and commuting corridors across Sandy Hook, Connecticut. Swipe.

slides.title: Sandy Hook Center
slides.text: A walkable historic village hub along the Pootatuck River with sidewalks, local dining, and central community gathering spots.

slides.title: Lake Zoar Waterfront
slides.text: Public boat launch facilities and beach access at Eichler's Cove offer direct access to freshwater boating and kayaking.

slides.title: Paugussett State Forest
slides.text: Extensive trail networks follow the river bluffs, providing scenic forested paths and shoreline hiking alongside Lake Lillinonah.

slides.title: Treadwell Memorial Park
slides.text: Town park amenities include regulation athletic fields, public tennis courts, a community pool complex, and open pavilion space.

slides.title: Highway Commuter Access
slides.text: Direct highway entrance points connect travelers west toward Danbury and east toward Waterbury, Hartford, and shoreline routes.

slides.title: Village Tree Lighting
slides.text: A long-standing late autumn tradition where the community marks the start of the holiday season in the center.

caption:
Sandy Hook sits along the Pootatuck River and Lake Zoar in eastern Fairfield County.

Exploring Sandy Hook CT means understanding its distinct layout. The village center provides walkable local dining along the river, while Eichler's Cove offers resident access to Lake Zoar for boating and seasonal recreation.

Trail systems span across Paugussett State Forest along Lake Lillinonah, giving hikers miles of river bluffs. For regional travel, convenient highway access connects drivers quickly across the corridor.
